body: ### Problem 1st case, calling nvim_win_set_buf() on a file that has an existing swap file (from another nvim or a crash) shows press-any-key   2nd case, when running `:edit file` or `nvim file` and then pressing ESC, but this only happens when it's not a swap file from a running nvim process because that will show a W325 warning instead ← Pressing ESC instead of OERDQA ### Steps to reproduce 1st case, open a file that's been opened by another running nvim process with `vim.api.nvim_win_set_buf(0, vim.fn.bufadd("filename"))` Just run this twice, need to change `~/.local/state/nvim/log` if it doesn't exist ```sh nvim --clean --cmd 'lua require("vim._core.ui2").enable()' --cmd 'lua vim.api.nvim_win_set_buf(0, vim.fn.bufadd(vim.fs.normalize("~/.local/state/nvim/log")))' ``` ```lua -- Above runs this code require("vim._core.ui2").enable() vim.api.nvim_win_set_buf(0, vim.fn.bufadd(vim.fs.normalize("~/.local/state/nvim/log"))) ```   2nd case, edit a file with an existing swap file from a crash, dunno how you'd script this 1. Open a file and edit it without saving 2. Kill that process (`lua vim.cmd('!kill -9 ' .. vim.fn.getpid())`) 3. Open that file by starting nvim with `nvim filename` or running `:edit filename` in a running nvim 4. When there's a prompt asking you to Open Read-Only, etc. Press ESC instead. ### Expected behavior The 1st case should be like this(?), this is from copying that message and `vim.print()` it with ui2 on.   The 2nd case, I think treating ESC as (A)bort makes sense, but [O]pen Read-Only is prolly more useful. ### Nvim version (nvim -v) v0.13.0-nightly+26e3c18 ### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same? no ui2 in vim? ### Operating system/version NixOS 26.11.20260910.8ce4ef6 ### Terminal name/version Ghostty 1.3.2-dev+44f2a44-nix ### $TERM environment variable xterm-ghostty ### Installation Nix Flake from github.com/nix-community/neovim-nightly-overlay
